shadow.$description: Three shadow recipes, replacing the three-plus-one v0 accumulated. Each step is a claim about how far an element sits above the page, and the three exist because there are exactly three such claims worth making: resting on the page, lifted off it, and floating over it. They are restrained on purpose — a shadow is a depth cue, and once it is heavy enough to be noticed as a graphic it has stopped being one. Depth is also the least reliable signal the system has: it disappears on a dark ground and for anyone with reduced contrast, so nothing may depend on a shadow alone to be understood. Every step is a single layer of pure black at low alpha, offset downward only, which is the one lighting direction that stays correct when the interface flips to RTL.

100.$description: Resting. The element is part of the page and is separated from it, not lifted off it — a card in a list, a sticky header that has just begun to scroll. Tight and faint enough that it reads as an edge rather than as a shadow, which is why it can be used on every card in a long list without the page turning grey.

200.$description: Raised. The element has been picked up off the page and is temporarily above its neighbours — a hovered or dragged card, a menu attached to the control that opened it. Reserved for things that are lifted for a reason, so that the lift itself carries information.

300.$description: Overlay. The element is over the whole interface rather than over its neighbours — a dialog, a bottom sheet, a toast. The top of the scale: anything that needs to feel further away than this needs a scrim behind it, which is a separate mechanism and not a fourth shadow.
